questions.question_text: Which international body publishes the annual Human Development Report comparing countries based on health, education, and income?
questions.explanation: The UNDP evaluates countries using the Human Development Index (HDI), combining life expectancy, educational attainment, and Gross National Income per capita.

questions.question_text: Per Capita Income is calculated by dividing the total national income of a country by its total ________.
questions.explanation: Per Capita Income (or Average Income) = Total Income of Country / Total Population of Country.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Focus on the core definition of Income in chapter 1.

solution_key_3_part.part2_step_by_step_derivation: Evidence derived directly from text: Per Capita Income (or Average Income) = Total Income of Country / Total Population of Country.

questions.question_text: True or False: A country with a high Per Capita Income is guaranteed to have equitable wealth distribution and uniform high quality of life for all citizens.
questions.explanation: Per Capita Income is an average metric that hides wealth disparities; a high PCI can exist alongside extreme income inequality where a small elite holds most of the national income.

questions.question_text: Explain why developmental goals can differ and sometimes conflict between different groups of people in society.
questions.correct_answer: Developmental goals differ because individuals have distinct socio-economic backgrounds and immediate life needs. Goals conflict when progress for one group harms another, such as industrialists wanting dams for electricity while displaced tribals lose land and livelihoods.
questions.explanation: Socio-economic positions shape priorities; what serves industrial expansion may cause ecological and economic ruin for indigenous riverine populations.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Focus on the core definition of developmental in chapter 1.

questions.question_text: Based on state comparative data, Haryana has a higher Per Capita Income (₹2,36,147) than Kerala (₹2,21,904), yet Kerala has a significantly lower Infant Mortality Rate (7 per 1,000 vs Haryana's 30). What does this reveal about development criteria?
questions.correct_answer: It reveals that economic income alone is an incomplete indicator of human well-being. Non-material and social infrastructure—such as Kerala's state-funded primary healthcare and education systems—are vital for high human development.
questions.explanation: Monetary wealth cannot buy essential public goods (health, literacy, sanitation); comprehensive development requires strong public facility investments.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Focus on the core definition of state in chapter 1.

questions.question_text: Evaluate the statement: 'Groundwater depletion in agricultural states like Punjab and Western Uttar Pradesh is an example of un-sustainable development.' Support your answer with evidence.
questions.correct_answer: Groundwater extraction in Punjab and Western UP exceeds natural rainfall recharge rates. Pumping water beyond replenishment degrades aquifers permanently, threatening long-term agricultural productivity and violating inter-generational equity.
questions.explanation: Over-exploitation of renewable resources turns a renewable asset into a depleted one, demonstrating growth that compromises future generations' survival.

questions.question_text: Case Study: In State X, 90% of rural households access subsidized food grains via the Public Distribution System (PDS), while in State Y only 35% do. Analyze the impact of this divergence on child health and Body Mass Index (BMI).
questions.correct_answer: State X will exhibit lower rates of child malnutrition and healthier BMI levels because functioning PDS networks guarantee basic food security regardless of household income. State Y will suffer higher rates of undernourishment (BMI < 18.5) among low-income rural children.
questions.explanation: Public facilities cushion vulnerable populations against market poverty, showing that health outcomes depend directly on state welfare delivery mechanisms.
questions.hint_modal: Hint: Focus on the core definition of In in chapter 1.
